messages:
Ashley: Quick Q — how do we want SDKs to map API errors -> exceptions across languages? Specifically: auth failures, rate limits, streaming handshake timeouts. Also want consistent request-id surfacing in logs for debugging. Working on a PR and want alignment.

Sam: +1 on a small unified hierarchy. Proposal: base RedwoodAPIError -> AuthError, RateLimitError, StreamHandshakeError, ValidationError. Keep names idiomatic per language (Error vs Exception).

Sam: Example (Python sketch):
```python
class RedwoodAPIError(Exception):
    pass

class AuthError(RedwoodAPIError):
    pass

class RateLimitError(RedwoodAPIError):
    def __init__(self, retry_after: Optional[int] = None, request_id: Optional[str] = None):
        self.retry_after = retry_after
        self.request_id = request_id
        super().__init__(f"rate limited, retry_after={retry_after} rid={request_id}")
```

Lina: Re streaming handshake quirk — we see a handful of clients that never get the ACK frame; server returns 408-ish after handshake window. For those, StreamHandshakeError should include the HTTP status (if any), the raw handshake response body, and x-rid header when present. Example log we use in runtime: 
```
WARN  runtime.handshake - handshake timeout; remote=10.2.1.5 seq=42 x-rid=01H3FJZQZQZXYZ status=408 body=""
```
That x-rid is critical for tracing across infra.

Ashley: Nice, so two asks in the PR: (1) add the exception classes + mapping layer that inspects error_code from API payload and maps to the right subclass; (2) ensure SDKs surface X-Request-Id / x-rid from responses as a top-level attribute on exceptions (and include in __str__).

Mike: For Java/TS naming, can we unify by keeping language idioms but documenting canonical names? e.g., Java: RedwoodApiException -> RateLimitException; TS: RedwoodApiError -> RateLimitError. Otherwise ppl get confused when reading cross-language docs.

Sam: Yup, docs section + table listing mapping. Also: for rate limits include .retryAfter (ms) and .requestId properties across SDKs. For streaming handshake we should add a small state machine in clients: OPEN -> SENT_HANDSHAKE -> RECEIVED_ACK -> STREAMING; if no ACK within handshake_timeout, raise StreamHandshakeError with requestId and raw body. Backoff policy: jittered exponential with cap at 60s, and give up after 5 attempts by default.

Ashley: Anyone opposed to including a tiny debug logger line in SDK that prints the full handshake response at debug level (only). That helps ops without polluting prod logs. e.g.,
```
logger.debug("handshake response", {"x-rid": resp.headers.get("x-rid"), "body": resp.text})
```

Lina: OK but please redact tokens and PII — only headers/body length and x-rid are safe. Add test that asserts logs do not contain Authorization header.

CI-bot: build #7821 passed for branch feature/sdk-exc-mapping (tests: 412/412). :white_check_mark:

Mike: @Sam can you PTAL my review on the PR? left a comment about Java docs and example of using Retry-After header.

Sam: Will review this afternoon. Quick note: when mapping HTTP 429 with retry-after missing, set retryAfter=None and expose the raw_secs_hint if available from error payload (some models give a "backoff_seconds" field).

Ashley: Action items: Sam — add mapping + tests. Lina — add handshake logs + infra-side acceptance test. Mike — update Java naming doc section. I'll open PR checklist entry about request-id exposure. Thanks y'all :rocket:

Mike: ack.

Ashley: tagging for visibility: @here — any other concerns before I merge the RFC-ish PR?
